Interpretation limits

  • The full active universe is the primary research control sample. It contains current-membership and survivor/selection bias.
  • Bitcoin is reported as its own category. Ethereum remains in the full research universe.
  • “Winner” always means the highest historical Sharpe within a displayed period. It is diagnostic, never a parameter recommendation.
  • All horizon variants keep the same 3 ATR Chandelier trail so horizon is the primary changed dimension.
  • Long/short and long-only are separate fixed policies. Borrow fees, borrow availability, crypto funding, cash yield, portfolio sizing, and cross-market correlation are not modeled.
  • The production daily-return path books configured basis-point costs but does not book the ATR slippage estimate used in trade rows. Results inherit that engine behavior.
  • Crypto retains the app's 252-period annualisation. ETF proxies are not equivalent to futures, especially products with roll or structural decay.

Cross-sectional horizon profile

How to read

Sharpe compares return per unit of realised volatility. Turnover and average holding period reveal the economic meaning of “speed”: faster variants should trade more and confirm reversals earlier.

Which speed wins in different periods?

Fast-signal confirmation lag

For every new Fast 20/10 non-zero position, the experiment looks forward up to 126 bars for each slower horizon to hold the same direction. A zero-bar lag means it already agreed on the fast entry date.

Next research gates

  1. Keep the equal-horizon ensemble as the neutral benchmark; do not select the in-sample winner.
  2. Add pure exit-channel variants as a separate stop-architecture experiment.
  3. Add volatility-scaled position sizing only after the unscaled signal comparison is stable.
  4. Build a cross-asset portfolio only after borrow, funding, cash yield, and ETF-versus-futures limitations are explicit.
